required_fixes: Narrow claim ceiling to deterministic localhost Flask dev server with maximally-distinct status+body responses; remove or qualify product consequence that C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR are unblocked for distributed/production testing — not demonstrated beyond synthetic localhost substrate

Re-test C1 with same-status body-only permission change (e.g., 200 with reader vs admin body) and C2 with header-independent variation to make C4 (full >= max baseline) discriminating; current C4 is vacuous (1.0 >= 1.0) because status, body, and headers all change simultaneously and Content-Length is body-correlated

Fix measurement-validity reporting: do not report bootstrap 95% CI [1.0,1.0] / [0.0,0.0] as informative precision — with 1 unique fingerprint per state (effective N=1, 20 identical resamples) the CI is degenerate and within-state variance is zero; report effective distinct N and treat jitter as non-varying under deterministic responses

Add header-independence test: current B-HEADERS-ONLY achieves 1.0 only via body-correlated headers (Content-Length varies 22 vs 108, Content-Type constant); test condition where bodies and statuses identical but server-side state changes only independent headers (e.g., Cache-Control, ETag, Set-Cookie) to validate drift detection beyond body/status tautology

validity_findings.finding: All fingerprints within each state are byte-identical (1 unique fingerprint per state, 20/20 identical). Bootstrap with N=1000 on set size 1 resampling identical values yields degenerate CI [1.0,1.0] for positive conditions and [0.0,0.0] for null. CI contains 0.0 is tautologically satisfied but carries zero information about sampling variability. Jitter 50-150ms uniform has no observable effect on fingerprint. Effective sample size is 1, not 20.

validity_findings.finding: Permission escalation (403 {'error':'forbidden'} -> 200 {'role':'admin','access':'full','dashboard':'...'}) and session invalidation (200 {'role':'reader'} -> 401 {'error':'session_invalid'}) change status code AND body AND Content-Length simultaneously. This is the maximally-distinct response design. Any substrate returning status or body would achieve discrimination 1.0. The experiment therefore demonstrates that SQLite writes change HTTP responses, not that the full-vector fingerprint adds value beyond single-field baselines.
validity_findings.evidence: raw_observations.jsonl body_len 22 vs 108 for permission, 57 vs 28 for session; report.md 2.2 baselines all 1.0; result.json baseline_status_only_permission 1.0, baseline_body_only_permission 1.0, baseline_headers_only_permission 1.0; spec.json:positive_control expects 403->200+body
validity_findings.impact: C4 (full >= max baseline) passes vacuously (1.0 >= 1.0) on both conditions; cannot support product consequence that full vector is needed or superior. Same-status discrimination left untested (unresolved[3] in result.json)

validity_findings.finding: B-HEADERS-ONLY discrimination 1.0 is driven by Content-Length (22 vs 108, 57 vs 28) which is deterministically body-correlated. Excluded headers are Date, Server, X-Request-Id; remaining headers are Connection:close, Content-Length, Content-Type:application/json. No independent header variation is tested. Spec hypothesis claims standard headers contribute to discrimination but evidence shows headers are redundant with body.

validity_findings.finding: Flask development server (Werkzeug) on 127.0.0.1:19847 used, not production WSGI (gunicorn/nginx). Responses are deterministic static JSON with no dynamic fields, no concurrency, no TLS/HTTP/2, no ETag/Cache-Control/Set-Cookie variation. The substrate's ability to discriminate under realistic middleware variation (report.md 3.3 Not tested, validity_notes Flask dev server) is untested.

validity_findings.finding: Null control fresh (iat=now, exp 3600s) vs near-expiry (iat=now-3570, exp ~30s remaining) produces identical responses because server validates expiry but ignores remaining-time difference while both tokens valid. 30s window with 20 paired observations (~4-6s total) leaves ~24-26s margin, so tokens remain valid throughout execution as observed. Null passing is correct and expected but tests identical-code-path responses, not subtle header/metadata drift where bodies identical but headers vary. Report.md notes not tested.

claim_ceiling: NARROWLY BOUNDED: On Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT 2.14.0 HS256 + SQLite WAL on 127.0.0.1:19847 (Werkzeug dev server), with SQLite-backed role lookup (role not in JWT) and session validity checked via DELETE, the HTTP fingerprint substrate (status + body bytes + filtered standard headers excluding Date/Server/X-Request-Id, hash of status||body_bytes||sorted_headers) deterministically discriminates maximally-distinct writable controls: permission escalation via SQLite UPDATE users SET role='admin' (403 vs 200+admin dashboard, Jaccard 1.0, N=20 but 1 unique fingerprint per state) and session invalidation via SQLite DELETE sessions (200 vs 401, Jaccard 1.0), while reporting 0.0 discrimination for fresh vs near-expiry valid JWTs producing identical bodies/status (30s remaining window, ~6s observation window). Claim does NOT extend to: same-status permission changes, header-only drift, ETag/Cache-Control/Set-Cookie independent variation, production WSGI/nginx, concurrent load, HTTP/2/TLS, real browser DOM, CDN, or distributed multi-node freshness. C4 equality (full == body == status ==1.0) shows body/status alone already at ceiling; full vector adds no demonstrated independent information in this design. Bootstrap CI is degenerate and not inferential. Unblocks C-FRESHNESS/C-DELTA-REPAIR only as localhost synthetic measurement substrate, not as distributed production infrastructure.
